findings.title: Error message 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' is misleading
findings.body: When a user submits a SQL expression query, ReadQuery now rejects it with the error "sqlExpressions is not implemented". The feature is in fact implemented but deliberately disabled as the CVE-2024-9264 mitigation, and the sqlExpressions feature flag still exists in the codebase. Users who explicitly enabled the flag will receive a message claiming the feature does not exist, which is confusing and makes support/debugging harder. The message should state that SQL expressions are disabled (e.g. "sqlExpressions is disabled") rather than not implemented.

findings.title: No regression test covering the SQL expression disable
findings.body: This PR disables SQL expressions as a security mitigation (CVE-2024-9264) but adds no test asserting that a query with type 'sql' is rejected by ReadQuery, nor that NewSQLCommand/SQLCommand.Execute fail with the stubbed DB now that go-duck is removed. Existing tests in pkg/expr/sql that exercised TablesList against a real DuckDB would now fail or have been silently affected, and there is no guard preventing a future change from accidentally re-enabling the execution path. A regression test verifying SQL expressions return an error would protect the security fix.
